# QS-CFW-4376-34 — Quality specification - valve body CFW-4376-34 (F316)
Revision: Rev C  
This revision supersedes Rev B.  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-4376-34

Scope
- This quality specification applies to the finished forged valve body CFW-4376-34 manufactured in Plant P3 from material F316. It defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, handling of nonconforming product, and the records required to demonstrate compliance to the requirements listed below.
- The document covers dimensional and metallurgical acceptance for the valve body CFW-4376-34 and applies at final inspection after all machining and heat treatment operations are complete.

Requirements table
- The table below lists the critical characteristics for valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34). These characteristics are controlled and recorded for every production lot.

| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness range (HRC) | 28-32 HRC | Must fall within 28-32 HRC on representative samples per lot |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.10 mm | Feature must be within nominal bore ±0.10 mm |
| Maximum forging weight | 46.2 kg | Forging weight must not exceed 46.2 kg as stamped or calculated |

- Rationale: Hardness range 28-32 HRC is specified to ensure the balance of strength and machinability for F316 valve bodies. Bore diameter tolerance ±0.10 mm is set to ensure sealing surfaces and mating components meet assembly requirements. Maximum forging weight 46.2 kg constrains forging dies and material flow to maintain mechanical properties and dimensional control.

Inspection method
- Sampling approach: Inspect each finished piece for dimensional conformance and record hardness on a representative sample selected from each production lot. Selection rationale and sampling records are described below.
- Dimensional inspection:
  - Measure the bore diameter with calibrated bore measurement equipment capable of reading to required precision. Confirm the measured value is within nominal bore ±0.10 mm. For clarity, record the nominal bore value on the inspection record and report the measured deviation relative to ±0.10 mm tolerance.
  - Inspect other critical mating features visually and by dimensional check to confirm they will not interfere with the bore requirement. When any feature affects the bore, include a note on the inspection record explaining the relationship.
- Hardness testing:
  - Perform hardness testing on a machined surface representative of the parent material, following surface preparation best practice to remove chips and scale. Record the hardness value and demonstrate compliance with 28-32 HRC.
  - Use a calibrated hardness tester appropriate for the expected hardness range and document calibration status on the test record.
- Weight verification:
  - Verify forging weight by the supplier stamping, weight ticket, or calculated material usage and confirm it does not exceed 46.2 kg. Record the source of weight verification on the inspection form.
- Measurement verification and equipment control:
  - Ensure measurement instruments and hardness testers are within their calibration cycle and traceable to accepted standards. List the instrument identifier and calibration status on each inspection record.
- Example inspection record entries:
  - Bore: nominal value, measured value, pass/fail versus ±0.10 mm.
  - Hardness: measured HRC, hardness test location, pass/fail versus 28-32 HRC.
  - Weight: documented forging weight source and pass/fail versus 46.2 kg.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation:
  - Any valve body CFW-4376-34 found outside the requirements in the requirements table must be clearly tagged, segregated from acceptable inventory, and logged into the nonconformance system. The log entry must reference the specific characteristic out of tolerance, the measured value, and the inspection record identifier.
- Disposition options:
  - Rework: Where the out-of-tolerance condition is dimensional and can be corrected by documented machining operations without affecting critical characteristics, perform rework only after written approval by the responsible engineering authority. The rework plan must reference the inspected nonconformance and describe controls to prevent recurrence.
  - Reject: If the hardness is outside 28-32 HRC or the forging weight exceeds 46.2 kg and cannot be recovered to meet specification, the part shall be rejected and returned to supplier or scrapped as defined by material disposition rules.
  - Use-as-is by concession: A concession for use-as-is may be issued only by authorized quality personnel when justified by engineering analysis. The concession shall document the nonconforming characteristic, rationale for acceptance, any special marking or restrictions on use, and a reference to the inspection data that shows the deviation.
- Root cause and corrective action:
  - For repeated occurrences of the same nonconformance, perform root cause analysis and implement corrective action to control the process. Document corrective actions, responsible parties, and verification of effectiveness.
- Records to keep:
  - For every production lot, retain the inspection records that show compliance or nonconformance for bore diameter ±0.10 mm, hardness 28-32 HRC, and forging weight 46.2 kg. Include instrument identifiers and calibration evidence.
  - Maintain nonconformance records, disposition decisions, rework plans, and concession approvals in the document control system. Records shall reference the part CFW-4376-34 and the inspection record identifier.
  - Retain supplier weight tickets or stamping evidence when used for forging weight verification.

Background and step rationale
- The hardness requirement 28-32 HRC was selected to meet expected service loads while allowing final machining and sealing operation tolerances. The bore tolerance ±0.10 mm reflects interface requirements with mating seats and stems to ensure leak-tight assembly. Maximum forging weight 46.2 kg controls forging die life and thermal mass for heat treatment uniformity.
- Following the inspection methods above ensures that measurement variability is controlled and documented. Example situations include a bore marginally outside ±0.10 mm that can be corrected by finish machining with documented engineering approval, or a hardness value outside 28-32 HRC indicating heat treatment deviation that requires batch-level investigation.

End of specification.
